correctness.rationale: The primary tetrahedron calculation decomposes the graph into three rotation sectors and gives exact secular factors. For \(k\notin2\pi\mathbb N\), the common factor \(A(k)=(k^2+3)\cos^2(k/2)-1\) is zero exactly when \(\tan^2(k/2)=k^2+2\), and the sector-specific factor is zero exactly when \(k\tan(k/2)=\pm\sqrt3\). The two alternatives cannot coincide: squaring would force \(k^2=1\), inconsistent with the first equation. Monotonicity on each tangent half-period gives one \(A\)-root in each half and exactly one signed simple root in the appropriate half. Every \(A\)-root is simple in each of all three orthogonal sectors, hence multiplicity three; a signed root occurs in one sector, hence multiplicity one. At \(k=2n\pi\), direct reduced boundary systems have kernel dimensions \(2,1,1\), giving multiplicity four. The local cotangent/tangent expansions give the stated momentum and energy offsets. The inspected verifier independently reproduces root brackets, sector kernel dimensions and asymptotic scaling but is not the proof of the all-period result.
